## Controller 1.0.51 (80)
- **Mac launch fix:** Fixed a crash on launch on earlier macOS 27.2 beta builds caused by weak-imported `Date` comparison operators in the macOS 27.2 SDK. - **iOS Simulator:** Finds Xcode when Command Line Tools is selected as the active developer directory, and displays the active screen on two-screen simulators. - **Antigravity:** Updated the bundled Antigravity ACP binary to 1.4.1 and preserved compaction status rows. - **Worktrees:** Excludes path-bound build directories when cloning worktrees and cleans up DerivedData for removed worktrees.

## Controller 1.0.51 (79)
- **New: iOS Simulator.** The inspector has a Simulator tab that shows a live iPhone or iPad simulator from this Mac, with Boot, Shut Down, Home and Take Control. Click, drag, hold and type to use it directly. The screen streams from the simulator's own display at up to 60 frames per second, with no Simulator window needed. - **New: agents can use the simulator.** Threads with Device access get on-demand simulator tools: pick a simulator, open apps, read the screen's elements, tap, type, swipe and take screenshots the model can see. Each thread drives only the simulator it selected, and taking control yourself pauses the agent. Tool rows summarize what happened without showing what was typed. - **Memory:** Memory keeps accepting new notes when its index grows large. Sessions now load the first part of MEMORY.md, with a pointer to the rest, instead of refusing a longer file, and memory consolidation no longer stops once the index fills up. - **Agents:** Clearer, shorter guidance for models. Conversations are told when browser, WebMCP, pull request, memory or Connect access becomes unavailable.

## Controller 1.0.51 (78)
- **Performance:** Threads write far less to disk. Streaming replies, tool output and many parallel subagents now save in fewer, larger batches, which is easier on your SSD and keeps busy sessions responsive. - **Performance:** Checkpoints and worktree lists no longer pause the app. Checking files for a checkpoint happens off the main thread, and worktree size scans are incremental, cancelable and limited in how many run at once. - **Fix:** Rolling back to a checkpoint could silently leave a newer version of a file in place if it was edited right after the checkpoint. Rollback now restores it reliably and leaves your staged changes alone. - **Agents:** Finished reports from many subagents reach their parent in one saved batch, and a report that could not be saved is retried instead of lost. - **Remote:** Sending from iPhone, iPad or Android while another send is in flight now joins it instead of failing.
